objective: Resolve a scenario by the exact (scenario_id, scenario_version) pair instead of indexing by scenario_id, so a second registered version no longer hides the first.
decision_supported: Should the registry index entries by scenario_id alone, or by the full identity the caller is required to name?
acceptance: resolve() with an explicit version returns that version's entry for every registered version.
resolve() with an unregistered version reports a mismatch and names the versions that are registered.
resolve() without a version stays ambiguous when the id has more than one version.
resolve() without a version still returns the entry when the id has exactly one.
describe() uses the same exact lookup.
Every registered identity resolves to itself.
evidence: Before the change, registering 1.0 and 2.0 and calling resolve('sample-scenario', '1.0') raised SCENARIO_REGISTRY_VERSION_MISMATCH claiming the id is registered at 2.0, even though 1.0 was registered.
After the change both versions resolve exactly, an unregistered 3.0 lists ['1.0', '2.0'], and the no-version call still reports SCENARIO_REGISTRY_AMBIGUOUS_ID.
tests/unit/test_scenario_registry.py: 65 passed, including six new cases.
stop_conditions: A caller depends on resolve() silently returning the last registered version; that is the implicit upgrade the registry documents it refuses.
risks_and_fallbacks: The index is now keyed by a tuple, so a duplicate (id, version) pair would collide. load_registry already rejects duplicate identities before constructing the registry.
_paths.py now orders libs/kernel ahead of libs/application because both contain a workbench package and the callers import workbench.kernel.
